output.title: What seasonality hides in a small business workflow
output.body:
Seasonality often hides a simpler problem: not demand, but visibility. When sales rise and fall, it is easy to miss the recurring work that keeps happening underneath — customer questions, invoice handling, data checks, or lead follow-up. That is the part worth looking at first.

For a small business owner, the practical decision is not “Should we automate everything?” It is “Which one repeating workflow still happens in slow months, and has a clear input, output, and correct result?” If you cannot point to the same task showing up week after week, AI is probably the wrong place to start. If you can, it may be a better candidate than seasonal firefighting makes it look.

A useful next step is to list 2–3 workflows that repeat regardless of season, then pick the one with the clearest observable measure: time spent, error rate, or approval delay. That is the workflow to review in a diagnostic before spending on tooling or hiring. Bareni’s approach is to identify one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and only then define the pilot scope. Money movement and other high-risk decisions still stay with a human — boring, but sensible.
